summary: This bill amends the Social Security Act to increase the negotiation period for certain drugs under the Drug Price Negotiation Program from 7 years to 11 years, making it effective as if it were part of the original law.

scores.thoughts: This bill directly amends the Social Security Act to change the negotiation period for drug prices under the Drug Price Negotiation Program. By extending the negotiation period for small-molecule drugs, it impacts the pharmaceutical industry and potentially drug costs, which is central to healthcare policy.

The bill delays Medicare drug price negotiation for small-molecule drugs from 7 to 11 years, reducing the savings generated by the Drug Price Negotiation Program and thereby producing smaller deficit reduction than under current law.

The sole purpose of the bill is to weaken the government's price-negotiation authority for small-molecule drugs by extending the pre-negotiation exclusivity period, shifting policy toward longer market-based pricing and away from government cost controls.
